first_pass.solution: Keep the bubble's words the same every time and put a small 'Note' or plus on it, so the bubble, my picture and the 'New note' menu row all look like the same thing.

test_cases.what_to_try: On the home screen, press your blank 'You' picture, below the bubble, and see what opens. Close it with its X; don't type and don't press Share. Then press the bubble itself and compare. Finally, press the pencil-square at the top right and look at the 'New note' row there; you may press it, then close.
test_cases.real_if: You'd never have guessed the picture makes a note, or the changing bubble words make it feel like different things.
test_cases.not_real_if: Once tried, it is obviously one thing in different places.
test_cases.what_happened: Pressing my blank 'You' picture opened a 'New note' screen with my picture in the middle and a bubble saying 'Share a thought...'. It didn't open my story or profile like I'd expected. I closed it with the X. Pressing the 'What's up?' bubble opened exactly the same New note screen. The pencil-square opened 'New message', which has 'New note' as the second row under 'New story', and that also opened the same New note screen. So all three really are one thing, and once I'd seen the New note screen I recognised it each time. But the bubble has three wordings now: 'Drop a thought' and 'What's up?' on the home screen, and 'Share a thought...' inside. I'd still never have guessed that tapping my own face writes a note. (The phone was slow, so one of my close taps arrived late and opened the side menu and then Message requests. I backed out of both without changing anything.)
